phase_0.boundary_condition: The functional equation s to 1 minus s creates a hermetic vessel where the critical line Re(s)=1/2 acts as the sole axis of symmetry, containing all nontrivial zeros as fixed points and preventing any orbit from straddling the boundary.

⊢.justification: The void state representing the complex plane region 0 < Re(s) < 1 before the confinement of zeros is established.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor that defines the global symmetry s to 1 minus s, closing the system and enforcing the boundary conditions.

≻.justification: The forward morphism driving the nontrivial zeros toward the critical line, establishing the affirmative state of confinement.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism representing the hypothetical descent of a zero away from the critical line, testing the stability of the fixed point.

⋈.justification: The composition of the reflection symmetry with the zero distribution, linking the geometric constraint to the analytic behavior.

⊙.justification: The self-reference where each zero on the critical line is its own image under reflection, s equals 1 minus s, signifying the system is at the threshold of criticality.

∈.justification: The split into two arms: the T-arm where the zero is pinned on the critical line, and the F-arm where the zero attempts to straddle the line.

∋.justification: The reconstitution of the zero state where the conflicting arms (fixed vs. straddling) fuse into a single verdict, often B if the barrier is real.

⊤.justification: The evaluation of the affirmative arm where the zero remains a genuine fixed point under reflection, confirming the Riemann Hypothesis.

⊥.justification: The evaluation of the negative arm where the zero fails to remain fixed, implying a violation of the functional equation or a topological defect.

⊞.justification: The state where both confinement and potential straddling are held simultaneously, representing a genuine dialetheia if the off-line case is not vacuous.

⊡.justification: The permanent record of the zero's location on the critical line, acting as a topological invariant that prevents continuous deformation to a trivial state.

Drive the F-arm away from the critical line, testing the reverse morphism of instability.
Evaluate the F-arm to check if the zero can straddle the line without violating symmetry.
Compose the reflection symmetry with the zero distribution to link geometric and analytic constraints.
Hold both the fixed and straddling states simultaneously if the off-line case is not vacuous.
Rejoin the T and F arms to determine the topological protection of the zero state.
Anchor the system with the functional equation, closing the boundary and enforcing global symmetry.

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑥: The reflection symmetry $s \to 1-s$ creates a cyclic closure where each zero is its own fixed point on the critical line, preventing any orbit from straddling the boundary.
⊢=𐑦: The confinement of all nontrivial zeros to the critical line implies a scale-collapse where the boundary (the line) carries the full content of the bulk (the critical strip) losslessly, rendering surface and interior as a single register.
⊞=𐑙: The reflection symmetry $s \to 1-s$ fixing zeros on the critical line implies an equal symmetric pairing of conjugate states.
⊡=𐑭: The confinement of zeros to the critical line acts as a topological invariant (winding number) that prevents continuous deformation to a trivial state without closing the spectral gap or violating the functional equation.
⊙=⊙: The confinement of all nontrivial zeros to the critical line with real part exactly one half signifies the system is precisely at the threshold of criticality.
⊥=𐑫: The confinement of zeros to the critical line as genuine fixed points under reflection implies a topological protection that prevents any straddling or interconversion without global restructuring.
≻=𐑽: The reflection symmetry acts as a catalytic constraint that stabilizes the zeros on the critical line without altering their fundamental nature.
≺=𐑹: The reflection $s \to 1-s$ fixing every zero on the critical line establishes an exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry at criticality where the operation is its own inverse.
⋈=𐑐: The geometric constraint of the critical line and the fixed-point nature of the reflection enforce a deterministic, high-fidelity interaction with near-certainty.
⊤=𐑧: The confinement of zeros to the critical line as fixed points under reflection implies a rigid, kinetically frozen state that resists rearrangement without external driving.
∈=𐑔: The reflection symmetry $s \to 1-s$ links every zero to its counterpart across the entire critical line, implying a global, scale-free correlation where the constraint on one zero affects the distribution of all others.
∋=𐑝: The requirement that the real part be exactly one half and the reflection symmetry pin each zero as a fixed point implies a strict conjunctive condition where all constraints must be satisfied simultaneously.
